status: DECLARED before the governing leave-one-month-out run (tools/run_pop_signals.py); exploratory scratch reads on the same months are disclosed below
purpose: The v9 LIRF schedule-fill mixture (configs/lirf_mixture_v1.json) sets the value of the LIRF population rows (no NM clock, no airport aircraft type; 383 ranking rows, 372 with a schedule interval at or below 43,200 s). On the four development months those rows carry 6-28% of the stack's squared error and a perfect fill/normal separation would remove about half of it. v9's classifier reads the row's own clocks and the timing of the previous arrival in-block at the stand. This round adds what that arrival is (same operator prefix, planned turnaround, its own block source, its NM record) and a leave-one-month-out callsign fill share, and re-fits the same three-class classifier bagged over eight seeds on twelve months.

control.description: v9's seventeen classifier features, the same protocol and seed bag; the shipped v9 classifier itself is one seed on January-November and cannot be scored leave-one-month-out

cs.description: control + cs_rate (callsign fill share over the other fitting months, smoothed)

cs_pa.description: control + cs_rate + the four previous-arrival features

callsign_rate.definition: (fills of the callsign in the other fitting months + 3 * overall fitting fill share) / (rows of the callsign in the other fitting months + 3); within a fold the training rows exclude their own month and the held-out month, the held-out rows use the eleven training months; the export uses all twelve 2025 months for the ranking rows

scope: population rows with a schedule interval at or below the mixture threshold (43,200 s); rows above it are outside this round (v40's fill pins and the three unpinned rows stay exactly as uploaded)
protocol: leave-one-month-out over the twelve 2025 months: classifier (v9's params, inner date-grouped folds for the round count, one booster per seed, mean probability) and normal component (v9's band medians) fitted on the other eleven months' population rows; held-out mixture = p_fill * interval + (1 - p_fill) * normal with p_fill = P(fill) / (P(fill) + P(normal)); squared error against the held-out label

rule.selection: among candidates whose twelve-month in-scope mixture SSE is at least 3% below the control's, that beat the control in at least 8 of 12 months and whose paired-month bootstrap 95% interval of the relative SSE change lies below zero, the lowest SSE; otherwise nothing
rule.note: a candidate that passes is still a change concentrated on a few hundred rows whose 2026 behaviour no development month can score (v10's day-density classifier passed the folds and lost 0.52 s); the user decides on any upload

export: v42 = uploaded v40 + 0.75 * (mixture_selected - mixture_v9_shipped) on the in-scope ranking population rows, floored at -12 s; every other row byte-identical to v40. mixture_selected: the selected candidate fitted on all twelve 2025 months with the declared seeds; mixture_v9_shipped: the mixture column of runs/lirf_mixture/export_v9/population_predictions.parquet (v9 = 0.25 * v7 + 0.75 * mixture on those rows, reproduced exactly). The 0.75 weight is v9's selected mixture weight, unchanged.

prior_exploration_disclosed.when: 28 September 2026, 10:15-10:45 UTC, scratchpad scripts on the same twelve months (no ranking label exists)
prior_exploration_disclosed.caveats: the scratch cs_rate excluded only the row's own month, so training rows saw the held-out month's fills in their feature (the declared tool excludes both); 279 of the 383 ranking population callsigns never appear in the 2025 population, so cs_rate is mostly the prior there; the previous-arrival prefix share is the same on the ranking (0.875) as in 2025 (0.88); a same-month operator arrival fill rate and the month arrival fill rate were explored and are not declared (unstable by month)
prior_exploration_disclosed.closed_alongside: LIRF clock-present fills (new inputs move AUC 0.885 -> 0.894, an explicit mixture still worse than the trees' hedge in every blend), hedge bias by delay band (none), no-NM long-interval rows outside LIRF (labels ordinary), arrival taxi-in context (residual correlation 0.004), LTFM block-clock structure (near its clock floor), block source census (only LIRF has schedule fills of any weight)
